title: Identification and Validation of Oxidative Stress-Related Candidate Biomarkers for Preeclampsia via WGCNA and Single-Cell Transcriptomics.
journal: American journal of reproductive immunology (New York, N.Y. : 1989)
one_liner_zh: 该文通过WGCNA和单细胞转录组筛选子痫前期氧化应激相关生物标志物，虽涉及转录因子调控预测，但核心是表达谱与诊断模型，无蛋白质-DNA互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Preeclampsia (PE) is a major pregnancy complication that poses risks to both the mother and the fetus. Oxidative stress (OS) plays a crucial role in its pathogenesis. This study aims to explore the diagnostic value of oxidative stress-related genes for PE. METHODS: We integrated single-cell and batch transcriptome data from the GEO database. Through differential expression analysis, WGCNA, and three machine learning algorithms (LASSO, SVM-RFE, and random forest), we screened key genes, constructed a diagnostic model, and analyzed its correlation with immune cells. We used bioinformatics tools to predict regulatory networks. The diagnostic value of key genes was verified through qRT-PCR experiments. RESULTS: Our study identified three hub genes-SPP1, CTSC, and SLC9A9-which were predominantly highly expressed in macrophages. The Hub gene and diagnostic model showed preliminary discriminatory ability in distinguishing PE samples from control samples in multiple datasets. Immune infiltration analysis demonstrated a strong positive correlation between macrophages and the three hub genes. Furthermore, cell adhesion emerged as a key signaling pathway in PE progression. FOXC1 was a common transcriptional regulator of all three hub genes, while FOXL1, NFKB1, and POU2F2 co-regulate SLC9A9 and SPP1. qRT-PCR validation confirmed the downregulation of these hub genes in PE. CONCLUSION: This study successfully identified SPP1, CTSC, and SLC9A9 as candidate biomarkers for PE, which may lay the foundation for the development of new monitoring indicators and optimization of targeted therapy strategies.
abstract_zh: 背景：子痫前期（PE）是一种主要的妊娠并发症，对母亲和胎儿均构成风险。氧化应激（OS）在其发病机制中起着关键作用。本研究旨在探讨氧化应激相关基因对PE的诊断价值。方法：我们整合了来自GEO数据库的单细胞和批量转录组数据。通过差异表达分析、WGCNA以及三种机器学习算法（LASSO、SVM-RFE和随机森林），我们筛选了关键基因，构建了诊断模型，并分析了其与免疫细胞的相关性。我们使用生物信息学工具预测调控网络。通过qRT-PCR实验验证了关键基因的诊断价值。结果：我们的研究确定了三个枢纽基因——SPP1、CTSC和SLC9A9——这些基因主要在巨噬细胞中高表达。枢纽基因和诊断模型在多个数据集中显示出区分PE样本与对照样本的初步判别能力。免疫浸润分析显示巨噬细胞与三个枢纽基因之间存在强正相关。此外，细胞粘附成为PE进展中的关键信号通路。FOXC1是所有三个枢纽基因的共同转录调控因子，而FOXL1、NFKB1和POU2F2共同调控SLC9A9和SPP1。qRT-PCR验证确认了这些枢纽基因在PE中的下调。结论：本研究成功识别出SPP1、CTSC和SLC9A9作为PE的候选生物标志物，这可能为开发新的监测指标和优化靶向治疗策略奠定基础。
